notes.text: Arise — A word of encouragement accommodated to the Jewish, or Hebrew style, wherein, as by lying down, is described a servile and calamitous condition, chap. xlvii, 1, so by rising, and standing up, a recovery out of it, into a free, and prosperous one, as may be seen frequently; Rouze up, intimating her deliverance to be at hand. Here under a type, of Jerusalem's restoration, is displayed the flourishing state of the Gentile - church, under the Messiah. Thy light - Thy flourishing and prosperous state.

The darkness — All kinds of errors. The Lord - Christ. Shall be seen - Shall be conspicuous; as the Lord's arising, to the darkness covering the earth, so the glory being seen, answers to that gross darkness.
The Gentiles — A plain prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles.

See — With delight the multitudes of thy children running to thee. Flow - They shall flock together to behold such an amazing sight. Fear - Or stand amazed. Enlarged - Both with joy, and love. The abundance - The islands of the sea, the nations, shall turn to thee in religion, and affection. The forces - Or wealth.

The multitude — The treasure, that is brought upon camels. By these, and such like figurative expressions in several verses of this chapter is implied the coming in of all nations to Christ, and therefore they are brought in as presenting the chief commodities of their respective countries. Dromedaries - A smaller sort of camel. Ephah - The Midianites, and Ephahites dwelt beyond Arabia. Sheba - A country in Arabia Felix, whose queen it was, that came to visit Solomon, and her bringing gifts might be a type of this, Solomon being a type of Christ. Gold - The principal commodities with which this country abounded, by which we are to understand whatever is precious.

glossa.text:
*Arise, be enlightened. (HIER)*. These things the Jews refer to the time of their own Christ, etc., *as far as* that at least on account of these things they may receive the Son of God.

*Arise.* ((ID.)) In the Churches, thou who didst go down in the synagogues: arise among the Gentiles, thou who didst fall among the Jews. Arise by confession, by the virtues, thou who didst fall by trafficking, by vices; and when thou hast arisen, be enlightened, that is, receive the faith of Christ.

*Light.* Promised to thee long before as about to come for thy redemption, which *enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world,* namely he who says: *I am the light of the world ((Joan. I, VIII))*, by whom thou shalt be enlightened if thou hast received the faith of Christ.

*The glory of the Lord.* For enlightening. The Son, namely, just as the risen sun enlightens the world; in figure of which the glory of the Lord was shown to Moses and to Solomon, the one building the tabernacle, the other the temple. The glory of the Lord also was the raising of the dead man, the cleansing of the leper, and things of this kind.
*The earth.* ((ID.)) The Jews, who love earthly things, to whom it is said: *You shall eat the good things of the land,* which they take carnally.

*Of thy rising.* ((ID.)) Because, that is, thou wast born of water and of the Holy Spirit, we all walk in the brightness of the rising of the primitive Church, because we have the same faith, and are born again by the same baptism.

*Lift up thine eyes round about.* To which is like: *Lift up your eyes and see the countries, for they are already white unto the harvest ((Joan. IV))*.

*Thy sons.* ((HIER.)) Whom thou hast begotten in the faith: Whence Paul: *Through the Gospel I have begotten you ((I Cor. IV))*. The first believers from among the Jews, when the Holy Spirit was given, *there were in Jerusalem religious men out of every nation which is under heaven ((Act. II))*, or the Gentiles from all the parts of the world.

*They shall come from afar.* Because they were far from God through idolatry, whence: *You who were far off, are made nigh ((Ephes. II))*.

 *From the side.* ((ID.)) Certain codices have, etc., *as far as,* nor does Jerome's sense incline to this.

*Of camels.* The camel is a humped and burden-bearing animal. These are the rich, carrying the burden of riches and the hump of sins.

*Dromedaries.* Dromedary or dromas, for it is called both ways: for it is an animal smaller than the camel, but swifter, in which are figured the Gentiles running swiftly to the faith.

*Madian and Epha.* Regions across Arabia abounding in camels and dromedaries, etc., *as far as* which is figured by the frankincense, they offered to the Lord.

notes.text: Judgments — He saith judgments in the plural number, because though the office of judging and ruling was but one, yet there were divers parts and branches, of it; in all which he begs that Solomon may be directed to do as God would have him to do.
Thy afflicted ones — For such are thine in a special manner, thou art their judge and patron.
The mountains — Which are so dangerous to passengers, in regard of robbers and wild beasts. Hereby it is implied, that other places should do so too, and that it should be common and universal.
Judge — Vindicate them from their oppressors.

Thee — Thee, O God, this shall be another blessed fruit of this righteous government, that together with peace, true religion shall be established, and that throughout all generations, which was begun in Solomon's days, but not fully accomplished 'till Christ came.
He shall come — Christ did come down from heaven, and brought or sent down from heaven his doctrine, (which is often compared to rain) and the sweet and powerful influences of his spirit.

glossa.text: *Unto Solomon,* etc. ((AUG.)) The true peaceable one, etc., *as far as* he who is here commended according to each nature. ((CAS.)) The fourth psalm concerning the two natures of Christ admonishes that we should believe Christ, true God and true man, to be king, and it is a prophecy about Christ.

*O God, judgment.* ((CAS.)) Concerning the judgment, in wishing that it be given to the Son. *Thy justice,* etc. ((AUG.)) Note that repetitions of the same thing, or in other words, greatly commend the divine utterances, which are chiefly in the psalms: and in that kind of speech by which the affection of the mind is to be moved.

*Mountains.* ((AUG.)) The Prophets, the Apostles, who by their height come near to heaven; *peace* to be announced to the faithful people, Christ. *And the hills.* Let them receive *justice,* that is, Christ, or *the mountains peace for the people:* and *hills* he says of both sorts of preachers, those going before and those following. Or *let the mountains receive,* that is, the greater ones.

*Peace.* The word of reconciliation, namely the word of the Gospel, to this end, that they may announce it to the people.

*And the hills.* That is, the lesser ones; justice, that is, obedience, that they may obey the teaching of truth.

By saying *thine* and *thy own,* he shows that all things which are the Father's are the Son's also, and conversely.

*He shall judge the poor of the people.* ((CAS.)) He treats the same matter concerning the same judgment, by affirming it. After the wish, by the power of prophecy, he says what things are to be furnished at the Lord's coming. ((AUG.)) Or according to another reading: *Justice shall judge the poor man.* But those codices which have [it] in the letter are the more approved. *The poor of the people.* That is, those who are poor among the people, in which the good and the bad are mingled together. *He shall humble the calumniator.* For while he helps by his grace, etc., *as far as* he who strives to drag the innocent into guilt. ((HIERON., AUG.)) Or, *he shall humble,* and, the devil being conquered, *there shall remain with the sun* a brightness; that is, the Son with the Father, sitting at the Father's right hand for ever, that is *before the moon,* unto generation and generation.

*He shall come down like rain,* etc. ((CAS.)) Behold who and of what sort is that king who is to judge. ((AUG.)) He alludes to the deed of Gedeon, etc., *as far as* and afterwards the Gentile world was rained upon, the fleece of the Jews being dry. ((CAS.)) Christ shall come down, etc., *as far as* who then, after such open likenesses, doubts of the Virgin's childbearing? *Into the fleece, and like drops.* ((AUG.)) *The fleece,* Judaea, which was to be despoiled of the authority of doctrine, as a sheep of its fleece: or, because it withheld the rain of doctrine, which it was unwilling to preach to the Gentiles.

notes.text: For this cause — That ye may be so "built together," I am a prisoner for you gentiles - For your advantage, and for asserting your right to these blessings. This it was which so enraged the Jews against him.
The dispensation of the grace of God given me in your behalf — That is, the commission to dispense the gracious gospel; to you gentiles in particular. This they had heard from his own mouth.
The mystery — Of salvation by Christ alone, and that both to Jews and gentiles. As I wrote before - Namely, chap. i, 9, 10; the very words of which passage he here repeats.

Which in other — In former, ages was not so clearly or fully made known to the sons of men - To any man, no, not to Ezekiel, so often styled, "son of man;" nor to any of the ancient prophets. Those here spoken of are New Testament prophets.
That the gentiles are joint-heirs — Of God. And of the same body - Under Christ the head. And joint-partakers of his promise - The communion of the Holy Ghost.
According to the gift of the grace of God — That is, the apostle- ship which he hath graciously given me, and which he hath qualified me for. By the effectual working of his power - In me and by me.

Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given — Here are the noblest strains of eloquence to paint the exceeding low opinion the apostle had of himself, and the fulness of unfathomable blessings which are treasured up in Christ.

What is the fellowship of the mystery — What those mysterious blessings are whereof all believers jointly partake. Which was, in a great measure, hidden from eternity by God, who, to make way for the free exercise of his love, created all things - This is the foundation of all his dispensations.
That the manifold wisdom of God might be made known by the church — By what is done in the church, which is the theatre of the divine wisdom.

By whom we have free access — Such as those petitioners have, who are introduced to the royal presence by some distinguished favourite. And boldness - Unrestrained liberty of speech, such as children use in addressing an indulgent father, when, without fear of offending, they disclose all their wants, and make known all their requests.

glossa.text: *For this cause,* etc. It having been shown that through Christ peace and reconciliation were made, here he sets down through whom they themselves were built together, because God revealed that salvation pertained to the Gentiles, and sent him to preach to them, and makes him suffer for them, that they may be the more pleasing to God.

*If yet you have heard.* That is, if you have understood the grace, that is, the apostleship dispensed by God, who knows why he chose me for this office? Or the apostleship, through which we weigh out diverse things to diverse men. By this he wishes them to know that by the judgment of God he was sent by Christ to preach to the Gentiles the mystery of the grace of God.

*As I wrote above,* etc. Namely, in that place *he is our peace.* For there he touched in a brief discourse upon the sum of the mysteries revealed to him, not so much bringing forth the whole that he knew, as showing it from a little.

*And to the prophets.* The earlier prophets indeed foreknew this of old concerning the Gentiles, that they were to be called, and to be partakers of the gift of God, but this lay hid, that without the law salvation would be theirs through faith in Christ.

*Through the Gospel,* etc. Through preaching the gift of God was made known, which God gives to the Gentiles according to the working of his power: by which he raised up Christ, in whom all are saved without the works of the law.
*A minister.* For it is not mine but God's, and so no thanks are to be rendered to me, but to God.
*Unsearchable.* By nature, namely, but through the grace and revelation of the Holy Spirit they are searchable to the faithful.

*Hidden from ages.* In the world are hidden the rational causes of all things which come to be naturally, as Levi was hidden in the loins of Abraham, when he was tithed. But in God are hidden the causes of those things which come to be through grace, or of those which, for the signifying of this, come to be miraculously and not naturally, which were done by the ministering angels. *In God.* For God has hidden in himself the causes of certain deeds, which he did not insert into created things, and he fulfils them, not by that work of providence by which he established natures that they might be, but by that by which he administers them as he shall have willed, which, as he willed, he founded. There also is the grace through which sinners are made safe. For not through a nature depraved by vice, but through the grace of God is man restored.

*That it may be made known.* It was given to me to preach the gospel and to enlighten. See how great this is, because through this something accrued to the angels, who learned many secrets in these things. *In the heavenly places.* Because there the Church was first, whither after the resurrection this Church also is to be gathered, that we may be equal to the angels of God.

*According to the predefinition.* For the wisdom which in its own nature is simple is, according to those things which are done in the world, which God predefined, that is, preordained, manifold, since it is varied in manifold ways. And lest the doctors of the sacred page should seem to contradict one another in the aforesaid opinions, what has been said can be determined thus: that to those who are of greater dignity, and by whose ministry those things were announced, they were known in part, as, for instance, to those familiars and messengers; but to those who are of lesser dignity, they were unknown.

notes.text: Bethlehem of Judea — There was another Bethlehem in the tribe of Zebulon. In the days of Herod - commonly called Herod the Great, born at Ascalon. The scepter was now on the point of departing from Judah. Among his sons were Archelaus, mentioned ver. 22; Herod Antipas, mentioned chap. xiv, and Philip, mentioned Luke iii, 19. Herod Agrippa, mentioned Acts xii, 1; &c., was his grandson. Wise men - The first fruits of the Gentiles. Probably they were Gentile philosophers, who, through the Divine assistance, had improved their knowledge of nature, as a means of leading to the knowledge of the one true God. Nor is it unreasonable to suppose, that God had favoured them with some extraordinary Revelations of himself, as he did Melchisedec, Job, and several others, who were not of the family of Abraham; to which he never intended absolutely to confine his favours. The title given them in the original was anciently given to all philosophers, or men of learning; those particularly who were curious in examining the works of nature, and observing the motions of the heavenly bodies. From the east - So Arabia is frequently called in Scripture. It lay to the east of Judea, and was famous for gold, frankincense, and myrrh. We have seen his star - Undoubtedly they had before heard Balaam's prophecy. And probably when they saw this unusual star, it was revealed to them that this prophecy was fulfilled. In the east - That is, while we were in the east.
To do him homage — To pay him that honour, by bowing to the earth before him, which the eastern nations used to pay to their monarchs.

The chief priests — That is, not only the high priest and his deputy, with those who formerly had born that office: but also the chief man in each of those twenty-four courses, into which the body of priests were divided, 1 Chron. xxiv, 6-19. The scribes were those whose peculiar business it was to explain the Scriptures to the people. They were the public preachers, or expounders of the law of Moses. Whence the chief of them were called doctors of the law.

Thou art in nowise the least among the princes of Judah — That is, among the cities belonging to the princes or heads of thousands in Judah. When this and several other quotations from the Old Testament are compared with the original, it plainly appears, the apostles did not always think it necessary exactly to transcribe the passages they cited, but contented themselves with giving the general sense, though with some diversity of language. The words of Micah, which we render, Though thou be little, may be rendered, Art thou little? And then the difference which seems to be here between the prophet and the evangelist vanishes away. Micah v, 2.
And if ye find him, bring me word — Probably Herod did not believe he was born; otherwise would not so suspicious a prince have tried to make sure work at once?
Seeing the star — Standing over where the child was.

They presented to him gifts — It was customary to offer some present to any eminent person whom they visited. And so it is, as travelers observe, in the eastern countries to this day. Gold, frankincense, and myrrh - Probably these were the best things their country afforded; and the presents ordinarily made to great persons. This was a most seasonable, providential assistance for a long and expensive journey into Egypt, a country where they were entirely strangers, and were to stay for a considerable time.

glossa.text:
*When therefore he was born,* etc. Although Matthew passes over the nativity, yet in relating the coming of the Magi he briefly commemorates it, saying thus: *When therefore. ((RAB.))* Four things are here set down, confirmed by the prophets, the nativity, the name, the place and the time, etc., *as far as* of the coming of the Magi Luke is silent, and Matthew sets it forth.

 *Bethlehem of Juda.* To distinguish it from that which is in Galilee, in the tribe of Zabulon. For there are two Bethlehems: Bethlehem was formerly called Ephratha; Bethlehem is the house of bread, because there the living Bread was to be born, who came down from heaven, who is laid in a manger: that having fed the irrational he may make them fellows of the angels. But it signifies the Church, which is the house in which the living bread is eaten.

*In the days. ((HIER.))* He sets this down not only for the time, but that it may be seen fulfilled, etc., *as far as* the Jews point out the place: the time of the coming they do not know.

((AUG.)) Jesus was made manifest not to the learned nor to the just: for it prevails, etc., *as far as* that no great man might be proud, no weak man despair.

 *They came.* The Magi, not after a year: because then he would not be found in the manger, but in Egypt, but on the thirteenth day. But they were from the land of the Persians, where also is the river Saba, from which the region is named, near which is Arabia also, where the Magi were kings. Who, although they are said to have offered three gifts, are not on that account proved not to have been more than three; but that through them the Gentiles which were born of the three sons of Noe, and were to come to the faith, might be prefigured: or there were so many princes, who led many in their train. Therefore the Magi make their request chiefly at Jerusalem: because through Balaam they had heard that he was to be born of Israel. For a new star was showing forth a new man. The star is Christ, whom we ought to follow, who unless he arise in our hearts, the king of the Jews is not sought in the East.

*Where is he that is born king,* etc. It is the confusion of the Jews, when they learn the nativity of Christ from the Gentiles, and if they do not believe, they are without excuse. *For we have seen his star.* This star, the herald of the Lord's nativity, never appeared before, but the child then created it and assigned it to the Magi: which soon, its office performed, ceased to be. A mute star proclaims Christ not yet speaking; afterwards, when he spoke, the apostles announced him to the Jews, as to those using reason; a rational substance, that is, an angel, announced the birth of Christ. But an irrational thing, that is, a star, led the Magi, the firstfruits of the Gentiles, not yet using reason. To the shepherds angels, to the Magi a star, yet to both the tongue of the heavens speaks, because the tongue of the prophets was already ceasing. Whether the star arose in the east, or whether they, being placed there, saw it risen toward the west, is doubtful. For it could arise in the east, and lead them to Jerusalem. But while they seek human help, as it were from the law, they are forsaken by the divine. By the star they understood that he was born in Judaea, and therefore they come to Jerusalem, where, learning the place and then setting out upon their journey, they first have the star going before them, which they recognize.

Allegorically. The star is the illumination of faith which leads to Christ. While they turn aside to the Jews, they lose it: because while they seek counsel from the wicked, they lose the true illumination.

((LEO.)) Three men follow the leading of the light from above, accompanying with intent contemplation the token of the brightness that went before them, to the acknowledgment of the truth, etc., *as far as* that the mystery of so great a vision might not lie hidden from them, and that what was shown to their eyes as unwonted might not be obscure to their minds.

*But Herod hearing,* etc. He is called king, that by comparison with him who is sought, this one may be understood a stranger, because the proper one had already failed.

*But Herod hearing.* That another king of the Jews than himself was sought; for, being a foreigner, he wished to seem the lawful king: and therefore he burned the records in which the genealogy is woven.

*He was troubled,* etc. Either because he fears the end of his kingdom, or on account of the wrath of the Romans if he should allow this, who had decreed that no one should be called king or lord without their counsel. The king of heaven being born, the king of earth was troubled, because assuredly earthly height is confounded when heavenly loftiness is proclaimed.

*With him.* Because of favour: because often the people the more unjustly favour those whom they endure as cruel. Whence Solomon: *A king* unjust *has all his ministers wicked ((Prov. XXIX))*.

*And assembling all the chief priests.* Note the diligence of the inquirer, that if he should find him he might do what he afterwards showed himself to wish: but if not, that he might be excused to the Romans. He was also probing whether their king would make the Jews sad or glad. *Where Christ should be born.* From the Jews he asks the place, from the Magi the time, that he may be made certain of both.

*In Bethlehem of Juda.* They express the place of the nativity, which by the testimony of Scripture they had learned, so that their very knowledge might become for them a testimony of damnation, for us a help to faith.

From this it is clear that not from ignorance, but from hardness of heart, they refused to believe.
*And thou, Bethlehem.* He sets this down as it was said by them, because although they do not set down the words, they do in some manner set down the truth of the sense.

*The Magi being called privately.* The priests and scribes being removed; for he feared lest the Jews should hide the promised one as by an oracle of God, if they should perceive that he wished to destroy him. Therefore also he promised that he would adore him, lest any should perceive his guile: but that without suspicion, for the favour of his good will, they might bring him word.

*That I may adore him.* Herod promises devotion, but sharpens the sword: painting the malice of his heart with the colour of humility. He feigned by countenance and by words to adore him whom with envious mind he was planning to kill. Whose person the hypocrites represent, who seek God feignedly, and never deserve to find him.

*And behold the star which they had seen.* Having entered Judaea they are forsaken by the token of the star, that they may be compelled to inquire from the law. Or they who seek human help are forsaken by the divine. Nor was it fitting that a sign given to unbelievers should appear to those of the household of the law and the prophets; because, *if they hear not Moses and the prophets: neither if one from the dead,* etc. It did not keep the paths of the upper air: but being very near the house, otherwise they would not have distinguished the house.

Morally. The star is a good exhortation leading to Christ. Or rather faith, which is the illumination of the mind, through which he who enters sees Christ, who is the morning star: and having seen him he rejoices with joy and does not cease to adore.

*They rejoiced with a great joy,* etc. He rejoices with joy who rejoices for the sake of God (who is the true joy). He adds also "great," than which nothing is greater. And "they rejoiced exceedingly," because of a great thing one man can rejoice more, another less.

VERS. 11. *And entering the house,* etc. Three Magi come by one journey to adore God: because in the one Christ (who is the way) the inseparable Trinity was to be adored by them. *The child with Mary his mother,* etc. Often is he named a child, that they may recognize him of whom it was said: *A child is born to us.* 

Why was not Joseph also found with Mary by the Magi? Lest any occasion of evil suspicion should thence be given to the Gentiles, who sent their firstfruits to adore him as soon as the Saviour was born.

*They adored him.* Thus confessing him God, whom they understand to have been brought to be man, and about to die, which they show by the myrrh.

*And opening,* etc. They testify their faith by mystical gifts: the gifts closed are the faith of the heart; the gifts opened, etc., *as far as* or by these three there are intimated in the same Christ royal power, divine majesty, human mortality.

*And having received an answer.* As Moses, being silent, cried out, so these with devout affection were asking what the divine will might command. This answer is not made through an angel, but through God himself, because no other appointed the way of return, save he who says: *I am the way, the truth, and the life.* The child does not speak to them, lest the divinity be revealed before the time, and that the true humanity may be held. Whence also he is soon sent into Egypt: because faith had to be nourished unto the reward, and the life of doctrine must be prepared for the going. *By another way,* etc. In this a pattern is given to believers, that they may come devoutly to God: and that they may attend to what he commands, namely, that they return not to the devil: but that they may come by the paths of the virtues to their country, and that they who fell by despising may rise again by obeying.

((LEO.)) They adore in the flesh the Word, in infancy wisdom, in weakness power, and in the truth of man the Lord of majesty, etc., *as far as* because what was proper in the substances was not diverse in the person.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Arise, shine; your light has come.
The glory of the Lord rises upon us.
Wise men followed a star out of the east.
We have come to kneel before the King.
They opened their treasures: gold, frankincense, myrrh.
We bring him all that we are.
Come, let us worship the light of the world.
Glory to God. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Lift your eyes from the dark road and look up — there is a light in the east, low and steady, and it is moving, and it is meant to be followed.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
Over a land still wrapped in night, the glory of the Lord is rising, and the nations are streaming toward the brightness.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
Travelers from far countries kneel in a small house and open their treasures — gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
So bring what you carry and lay it down; the One the star pointed to is here.
Arise, shine; your light has come. Glory to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A light rises in the east; the dark gives way.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
The wise men follow the star to the child.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
They open their treasures and kneel down.
Arise, shine; your light has come.
Come, let us worship the light of the world.
Arise, shine; your light has come. Glory to God!
